title: Which graph should you draw?
caption: Two questions about the variables choose the graph. A categoric independent variable gives a bar chart; one continuous variable counted in classes gives a histogram; two measured variables with nothing controlled give a scatter graph.
alt: A flow chart of questions leading to a bar chart, a histogram, a scatter graph or a line graph.
description: Is the independent variable continuous? If not, draw a bar chart.
Are two different variables plotted against each other? If not, draw a histogram of the frequency of one variable.
Did you set the independent variable yourself? If not, draw a scatter graph to look for a correlation.

q1.q: Is the independent variable continuous, measured on a number scale?

bar.outcome: Bar chart: the independent variable is categoric (blood group, species)

q2.q: Are you plotting two different variables against each other?

hist.outcome: Histogram: the frequency of one continuous variable in classes, bars touching

q3.q: Did you set the independent variable yourself, in an experiment?

scatter.outcome: Scatter graph: look for a correlation between two measured variables

line.outcome: Line graph: independent variable on the x-axis, dependent on the y-axis
